correctness.rationale: Map every production to an edge of an acyclic multigraph with terminal sink. Every word is read along a source--sink path. Splitting p edges into r initial edges and p-r remaining edges bounds the path count by r*M(p-r), with M(0)=1, and layered parallel-edge graphs attain the integer-break recurrence for every positive budget. Equality analysis uses strict increase of M(p) for p>=2: all remaining edges must be reachable from each branch head, forcing a common head in a DAG, then the same argument inductively. Full-path label injectivity is necessary and sufficient. A unary mixed-radix label assignment generates every exponent 0..M(p)-1 exactly once, proving the inverse cover complexity. Two standalone checkers corroborate the recurrence for p<=24 and all small topologically ordered multigraphs with p<=9, but these finite tests are not used as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The source paper proves NP-completeness for general regular cover (Theorems 3.7 and 4.6), not the exact per-production maximal finite-language cardinality, equality-rigid directed multigraphs, or the all-parameter unary interval cover threshold. The previously published cardinality bound is \(2^{p-1}\) (Hetzl--Wolfsteiner 2019, Lemma 7), strictly weaker than the exact integer-break bound for \(p\ge3\) (for instance \(p=4\): the former is 8 while the latter is 4). The 2020 thesis reports only logarithmic regular descriptions of arbitrary unary languages; it does not assert the sharp constant, inverse threshold or equality structure. published-finding corpus comparisons found related unary automata and grammar-like state costs but no implication of this statement. The 1981 original and a 2026 all-path graph article were not fully accessible; the residual priority risk is stated and is not counted as a verified noncoverage result.
residual_risks: The full 1981 article was unavailable; a sharper unquoted capacity or structural lemma could reduce priority.
The 2026 Hajac et al. paper on all-endpoint DAG paths was available only in abstract/secondary summary; an internal single-terminal special lemma might cover part of the result.
Unindexed works describing the exact same source--terminal path bound or mixed-radix unary grammar may exist.
Grammar production models that count terminal letters rather than whole terminal strings differ and are not covered.

value.rationale: This is a sharp universal cardinality-per-production budget, not a restatement of the elementary integer-break exercise: the grammar-to-DAG inequality is exact, all equality *grammar structures* are classified, and a nontrivial unary mixed-radix labeling saturates the bound with a natural consecutive-length language. Consequently the regular-cover problem has an explicit sharp threshold for every unary interval, and its exact asymptotic leading constant is determined. The previous 2^(p-1) growth estimate is substantially loose (e.g. 32 versus 9 at p=6); this supplies a rigorous baseline and extremal test family for grammar minimization despite the general NP-completeness. It neither asserts a paper-sized downstream theorem nor claims hardness has been solved.
